industry.why: Neutral, carried, split. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): DNB Carnegie's new mining cycle and Danske's soft commodities up 10 to 40% since the second quarter are the demand side; Metals and mining relative strength falling to F from A, steel to D from B and cement to F from C are the tape, with energy costs at Brent $111 the margin squeeze. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior. Base chemicals, Steel and Cement carry D; Fragrances, Specialty chemicals and Forestry stay C.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the cyclical, energy-intensive end of materials into a growth scare with Brent $111; no steel price or materials strategist was read, so the condition for C is untested. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, B prior, agrees now. Four Pool names (Alleima, Grupa Kety, SSAB, ArcelorMittal), three of them leaving the Pool. Counter-case: the European Union's quota extension protects European steel, and steel bottoms before the growth data do.

geography.why: Neutral, from Overweight. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): the condition written on this row on 2-Oct-26 (it stays B only while the Banks row is Overweight) is no longer met, since Banks goes to Neutral on the credit tripwire; the Greek listings in the MI Pool are six banks plus Cenergy, HELLENiQ Energy and Motor Oil, with the live holding Ballys Intralot beside them, so the country letter was a second bank weight, and in a week when European sovereign stress is spreading from France to Italy and Spain a bank-heavy periphery listing is where contagion lands next, though Greek spreads themselves were not read. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case: Goldman Sachs's emerging market team (8 Oct) stays overweight Greece by name, Greece is not among the sovereigns named under stress, and the Greek energy names are on the right side of the regime; back to B if the Banks row returns to Overweight.
